chapter_title: The Building Blocks of Schools, Students, and Learning
learning_objective: The learner will explain which earlier concepts each Chapter 1 concept depends on by identifying its direct prerequisites in the chapter's concept map, correctly answering at least five of six prerequisite questions.
specification:
Type: graph-model **sim-id:** building-blocks-concept-map
**Library:** vis-network
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** explain
**Learning Objective:** The learner will explain which earlier concepts each Chapter 1 concept depends on by identifying its direct prerequisites in the chapter's concept map, correctly answering at least five of six prerequisite questions. **Template:** https://github.com/dmccreary/automating-instructional-design/tree/main/docs/sims/chapter1-concept-map
**Prerequisites:** all 21 concepts defined in this chapter, and the meaning of a dependency arrow (an arrow points from a concept to a prerequisite it depends on), defined in the section "Putting the Building Blocks Together" above. **Evidence of Mastery:** The learner answers six prerequisite questions by selecting nodes in the map. An answer is correct when the selected set exactly equals the direct-prerequisite set given in Content. Mastery is 5 of 6 correct. Clicking nodes to read definitions is exploration. **Misconceptions:** (1) The concepts are independent vocabulary words. (2) Advanced-sounding concepts (Higher-Order Thinking) must have many prerequisites. (3) Arrows point from a prerequisite to what it enables; in this book they point from a concept to what it depends on. **Instructional Rationale:** Explaining relationships is an Understand-level skill, shown here by locating each concept's prerequisites. Answering by selecting nodes in the actual graph forces the learner to read arrow direction correctly, which later chapters on learning graphs depend on. **Content:** Nodes (21), each with the one-sentence definition shown when the node is selected: | Node | Definition shown | |---|---| | Education | The organized, intentional effort to help people acquire knowledge, skills, values, and ways of thinking. | | Learning | A relatively lasting change in knowledge, skills, or understanding that results from experience. | | Student | A person enrolled in a course of study at an educational institution. | | Teacher | A professional whose job is to help students learn through planning, explaining, assessing, and feedback. | | School | An institution a society sets up to provide education to a defined group of learners on a regular schedule. | | Curriculum | The planned body of knowledge, skills, and experiences a school intends students to learn, and its sequence. | | Educational Technology | Tools, devices, software, and media used to support teaching and learning, with the practices for using them well. | | Classroom | The room, and the group of students and teacher within it, where scheduled instruction happens. | | School Day | The daily schedule of periods, transitions, meals, and breaks during which students attend school. | | Public School Funding | The system of revenues, mainly local, state, and federal taxes, that pays for public schools. | | Per-Pupil Spending | Total annual spending on public schools divided by the number of students enrolled. | | Learning Outcome | A specific, observable statement of what a learner will be able to do after instruction. | | Learning Gap | The difference between what a student is expected to know and what the student actually knows. | | Bloom's Taxonomy | A framework that classifies learning outcomes into six levels of cognitive work. | | Higher-Order Thinking | The cognitive work of the top three Bloom levels: analyzing, evaluating, and creating. | | Formative Assessment | Gathering evidence of learning during instruction and using it to adjust teaching and learning. | | Direct Instruction | A teacher-led method of explaining, modeling, guided practice, and independent practice. | | Spaced Practice | Spreading practice sessions over time instead of concentrating them in one session. | | Retrieval Practice | Learning by actively recalling information from memory rather than rereading it. | | Student Agency | The capacity and opportunity for students to make meaningful choices about their own learning. | | Self-Paced Learning | An arrangement in which each student advances through material at their own speed. | Edges (20), each pointing from a concept to a prerequisite it depends on: | From (depends) | To (prerequisite) | |---|---| | Curriculum | Education | | School | Education | | Educational Technology | Education | | Student Agency | Student | | Student Agency | Learning | | Self-Paced Learning | Student Agency | | Learning Outcome | Learning | | School Day | School | | Public School Funding | School | | Per-Pupil Spending | Public School Funding | | Learning Gap | Learning Outcome | | Classroom | School | | Direct Instruction | Teacher | | Direct Instruction | Learning | | Direct Instruction | Classroom | | Spaced Practice | Learning | | Retrieval Practice | Learning | | Bloom's Taxonomy | Learning Outcome | | Higher-Order Thinking | Bloom's Taxonomy | | Formative Assessment | Learning Outcome | Six questions, in this order: | # | Question | Correct selection | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Select every direct prerequisite of Per-Pupil Spending. | Public School Funding | You need to know where school money comes from before you can divide it per student. | | 2 | Select every direct prerequisite of Higher-Order Thinking. | Bloom's Taxonomy | Higher-order thinking is defined as the top three levels of the taxonomy. | | 3 | Select every direct prerequisite of Self-Paced Learning. | Student Agency | Letting a student control their pace is one form of giving them agency. | | 4 | Select every direct prerequisite of Learning Gap. | Learning Outcome | A gap is measured against an expected outcome. | | 5 | Select every direct prerequisite of Direct Instruction. | Teacher, Learning, Classroom | Direct instruction is a teacher leading a classroom toward learning; it needs all three. | | 6 | Select every direct prerequisite of Formative Assessment. | Learning Outcome | Formative assessment checks progress toward a specific outcome. | **Provenance:** Nodes and edges are taken from `docs/learning-graph/learning-graph.json` in this repository, restricted to the 21 Chapter 1 concepts; copy the values listed here into the sim rather than reading the file at run time. Definitions come from the chapter prose. **Rules:** Foundational nodes (Education, Learning, Student, Teacher) have no outgoing edges and must be visually distinguished as having no prerequisites. A question's answer is correct only when the selected set equals the correct set exactly (no missing and no extra nodes). The learner can zoom and reset the view with buttons; mouse-wheel zoom is disabled. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner explores the map, selecting nodes to read their definitions. 2. The learner starts the quiz. Question 1 appears; the learner selects one or more nodes and submits. 3. The sim marks the answer and highlights the correct prerequisite nodes and their edges. 4. The learner continues through question 6, then sees the score. 5. The learner should notice that Higher-Order Thinking has only one direct prerequisite even though it sounds advanced, and that four concepts have no prerequisites at all. **Feedback:** Six questions, fixed order, two attempts each. Correct: "Correct. [Why text]." Incorrect with missing nodes: "You're missing at least one prerequisite. Follow every arrow leaving [concept]." Incorrect with extra nodes: "At least one selected concept is not a direct prerequisite. Only count arrows that leave [concept] directly." After the second wrong attempt, the correct nodes are highlighted with the Why text. Score "n of 6" is shown at the end. **Starting State:** The full map of 21 nodes and 20 edges is shown, with no node selected, and the prompt reads "Every concept in this chapter rests on others. Which ones?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter states that it covers 21 concepts, that arrows point from a concept to a prerequisite it depends on, that Learning Outcome depends on Learning, that Higher-Order Thinking is defined by Bloom's Taxonomy, that Direct Instruction requires a Teacher, a Classroom, and Learning, and that Per-Pupil Spending depends on Public School Funding.
